parameters.disclosures: No realised outcome was re-drawn, kept or dropped because of its value. The designed relationships are built into the draws as parameters chosen BEFORE the first run (the fast team's delay scale is 900 minutes against 2,400; issues detected before 2026-08-25 are never left open; critical rules other than ds-customers' stop failing on 2026-09-20), and they came out as designed on the first run; nothing was tuned afterwards. | The sizes (rule runs and issues, see row_counts) are what the stated parameters gave; start offsets and the issue probability were set to reach 'about 4,500' and 'about 600' before looking at any other outcome. Two code changes altered the draws before the final run (a stray draw was removed from the rules stream, and the window kept free of rule-version changes around the weight change was widened from 7 to 14 days after the realised changes were seen to fall 8 to 14 days from it); the reported world is the first run of the final code and nothing was re-drawn after it. | Match precision, the households wrongly approved and the reversals are drawn from reviewer probabilities (true pair approved 94 %, household 25 %, near name 12 %; reversals weighted 8:1 towards wrong approvals); the realised values are reported, not steered. | The size cap of 5 MB did not bind: every count of the specification is met.
parameters.issue_probability: 600 expected issues over the failing scheduled runs, weighted by severity 30/14/10/6

synthetic_truth.note: Synthetic match truth for the verification layer only: it is never loaded by the matcher, the seeder or the API.
